subject: Symmetry Solutions — architecture playback & integration readiness
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.z@symmetry.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.p@symmetry.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2024 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood integration — high-level architecture and test plan

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team here at Symmetry is excited about Redwood's latency and routing features. Per our conversation, I wanted to share a concise summary of what we'd like to validate during a short partner integration spike next week and confirm a time for an architecture playback.

High-level goals:
- Validate token-level routing between our gateway and Redwood dedicated pool.
- Confirm prefix caching behavior for our conversational flows (~1.2k avg context).
- Exercise fallback to a lower-cost model variant under simulated capacity constraints.

Proposed acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end request RTT from Symmetry gateway to Redwood hosted endpoint below 180ms p95 for single-turn requests.
2) KV prefix cache hits for at least 30% of step-inferences during load test.
3) Graceful fallback observed with no >2s failed responses when primary pool is taken to 80% load.

I've attached a reference diagram (png) and a first-pass SOW we can iterate on. Can you and your solutions/serving folks join a 45-minute architecture playback on Thursday 17th at 10:00 PT? If that works we'll send calendar invites and list of test accounts.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Head of Platform Partnerships | Symmetry Solutions

Attachments: symmetry-reference-diagram.v1.png, sow-draft-symmetry-2024.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.z@symmetry.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.p@symmetry.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2024 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration — high-level architecture and test plan

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts. Yes — Thursday 17th 10:00 PT works for our team. I'll include our solutions and serving engineers on the invite.

Quick takeaways from my side so we can align expectations before the session:
- RTT target: we can likely meet 180ms p95 for single-turns on Dedicated in us-west with our optimized kernels; multi-turns with KV cache active will vary — bring representative sample prompts.
- Cache hit % will depend heavily on how you arrange prefixes; we can instrument metrics to report prefix hit ratio per endpoint.
- We'll demonstrate policy-based fallback (primary -> variant-small) and walk through the automatic rollout rules.

We'll use a short checklist in the playback: architecture diagram walkthrough, test data and accounts, load test plan, and rollback expectations. I'll loop-in internal folks.

See you Thursday,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Partner Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Sergio / Karthik / Ben — forwarding Symmetry's ask and the two artifacts. Can you review quickly before the Thursday playback? Key points to prepare:

1) Sergio — can you run the kernel/latency readout for our dedicated us-west config and confirm p95 single-turn expectations (small/medium/large model variants)? Include expected variance for ~1.2k context.
2) Karthik — we'll need the exact metrics we'll surface for prefix/KV cache hits and how to expose them to Symmetry (route-level dashboards + trace ids). Also confirm if we can carve a test-only route with increased retention for traces.
3) Ben — prep a short demo that shows fallback policy in action and the automatic rollback guardrails. Ideally a script we can run during the playback.

I'll attach the diagram and SOW in the playback invite. Let's sync for 20 minutes at 09:00 PT on Thursday if that helps.

—Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2024 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood integration — high-level architecture and test plan

Marissa / team — quick status: I put together a short scripted demo that runs three scenarios and toggles fallback via our rollout API. Notes:
- Scenario A: baseline single-turn requests (50 req/s) to large model variant — expected p95 ~150ms in us-west dedicated.
- Scenario B: conversation flow (simulated 6-turn convo, 1.2k avg context) with KV cache priming — we instrumented cache-hit metrics, expecting ~28-35% hits depending on prompt variability.
- Scenario C: simulate capacity constraint by driving the pool to 85% and trigger automatic fallback to variant-small. We'll capture error and latency profiles.

I uploaded the demo script and sample prompts to the shared drive folder and annotated the steps in the README. I can run the demo during the playback and hand off to Sergio for the latency readouts.

Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: demo-runbook.md, demo-script.sh

Subject: Re: Redwood integration — high-level architecture and test plan

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround and for scheduling the playback. Confirming a couple of logistics before Thursday's session:
- Test accounts: we'll provision two test routes from our gateway (staging-1, staging-2) and share API keys in a secure vault link ahead of time.
- Data: prompts are synthetic and scrubbed; we'll share a sample set of 120 prompts for the conversation flow.
- Success metrics: we'll accept p95 <= 180ms for single-turn on staging-1, and cache hit >= 25% for conversation flow. The fallback behavior demonstration is informational but we need no regressions in correctness.

If that's aligned, we'll send the credentials and the prompt set to the Drive link tonight. Looking forward to the playback — please send the calendar invite and dial-in.

Best,
Raj Patel
Director, Platform Integrations | Symmetry Solutions
